title: Part Two, Chapter 1: Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu

verses.t: And now we shall tell the name of the father of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque. Very obscure was their beginning, and very obscure is what is said and told of that Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque; and so we shall tell only half of what there is to tell of their father.

And this is what is told: the name of their father is Hun-hun-ahpu (that is, "each one a blowgun hunter"), and so they are called; and the parents of this Hun-hun-ahpu were Xpiyacoc and Xmucane. And these were born in the darkness of the night (that is, before there was sun or moon, and before man was created): they were Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu ("seven in one hunter"). And this Hun-hun-ahpu had two sons; the first was called Hun-batz (that is, "a spun thread"), and the second was called Hun-choven (that is, "one who is in order"); and their mother was called Xbaquiyalo (that is, "tied bones"), and she was the wife of Hun-hun-ahpu. And the other, Vucub-hun-ahpu, was not married, but stayed just as he was, like a youth. These were great sages and diviners, and their wisdom here on the earth was great, and their ways were very good. And Hun-hun-ahpu taught his sons Hun-batz and Hun-choven to play the gourd, to sing, to paint, to carve and to work precious stones like silversmiths. And Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu did nothing but play at dice and at ball; this was their pastime every day; they played two against two, all four together, when they gathered in the court. And the Voc (a certain bird) came there to watch them; he was the messenger of Huracán, Chipa-caculha and Raxa-caculha, and this Voc was not far from here, from the earth, nor was the underworld far for him; in an instant he reached the sky with Huracán; and they stayed here upon the earth. And the mother of Hun-batz and Hun-choven was already dead. And they were playing ball on the road to the underworld, and then Hun-came and Vucub-came heard them (that is, "one taker" and "seven takers"), who were lords of the underworld. "What is that being done on the earth? They are making it shake and making noise. Let someone go and call them; let them come here to play ball; let us beat them and destroy them, for they have no respect or fear of us, but are quarrelling over our heads." This is what all those of the underworld said. And then they all took counsel. They were called Hun-came and Vucub-came, and these were great judges; and all the lords who attended them, and served them and made up the kingdom of Hun-came and Vucub-came, were these: Xiquiripat (that is, "the flying eel") and Cuchumaquic ("gathered blood"), and their office is to cause the bleeding by which men fall sick. Others were called Ahalpuh ("he who makes the pus") and Ahalcana ("he who makes the dropsy"), and their office was to make men swell, to give them sores on their legs and to cause yellowness in their faces; this sickness is called chiizanal, that is, yellowness; and this was the office of Ahalpuh and Ahalcana. And another was called Chamiabac ("bone staff"), and another Chamia-holom ("skull staff"). These were the constables of the underworld, whose staffs were only bones, and their duty was to waste men away until, reduced to bones and skulls, they died, with nothing but their bellies stuck to their backbones; and this was the office of Chamiabac and Chamia-holom. Others were called Ahalmez ("he who made rubbish") and Ahaltocob ("he who caused misery"), and their office was to stab men, so that harm befell them and they died face down, at the door of the house or behind it; and this was the lordship of Ahalmez and Ahaltocob. And others were called Xic ("hawk") and Patán ("tumpline"), and their office was the sudden deaths of those who die on the roads vomiting blood; and each one's office was to load them up and pound their hearts when they died on the roads, and give them fluxes of blood; and this was the office of Xic and Patán. All these were those of the council, to pursue Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu. And what those of the underworld wanted was to see the gear of Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu: the leather shield with which they stopped the ball, the bat, the ring, the crown and the face-guard, which were the instruments with which they played and adorned themselves for the game. And now we shall tell of their going to the underworld. And their sons Hun-batz and Hun-choven stayed behind here, and their mother was dead. But this was before Hun-batz and Hun-choven were defeated by Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque.
